note:
The YOUNGER SELFIE variant of the three clinical-result blocks on /pages/acetyl-hexapeptide-8-research - templates/page.research-argireline.json, section `key_findings`, blocks f1, f2, f3. Malcolm, 2026-08-26: new models, aged thirty to forty, amateur, and make the pictures CLEARLY selfies. All earlier waves kept.

"CLEARLY A SELFIE" REQUIRED UNDOING ONE OF MY OWN RULES, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE FIX. The previous two selfie waves banned hands and arms from frame to keep the phone out of shot - which is precisely why several of them read as ordinary portraits taken by someone else. The raised near arm cutting into the bottom corner is the single strongest tell there is, so it is now REQUIRED rather than negated, alongside a camera that is deliberately not at eye level, harder wide-lens distortion on the nose and chin, a gaze aimed at the screen rather than the lens, a crooked horizon and off-centre framing. The phone itself and any mirror stay out - a visible phone adds clutter and occludes the face, and the arm alone carries the read.

⚠️ THE AGE CHANGE FIGHTS AN EARLIER INSTRUCTION AND MALCOLM WAS TOLD BEFORE THE WAVE RAN. He asked on 2026-08-25 that the percentage improvement be clearly SEEN. A woman of thirty-eight has fine, early expression lines rather than the deep set creases of the fifty-plus casting used in selfie r1 and r2 - so half the depth of an already-shallow line is a much smaller visible difference. The honest magnitudes are kept (f1 about half, f2 about a third, f3 the smallest), but the change will read subtler than in the older waves. That is a property of the casting, not a fault in the frames, and f3 in particular is now very subtle indeed.

AND IT ADDS A NEW WAY TO GO WRONG: the engines will reach for deep wrinkles because the brief is about wrinkles. A thirty-something with the creases of a fifty-something is the wrong woman for the age given, so the brief states outright that she has NO deep set wrinkles, no jowls, no sagging and no grey hair, and those are named in the negatives too. CHECK AGE PLAUSIBILITY FIRST ON EVERY CANDIDATE.

CARRIED OVER UNCHANGED:
  * THE HONESTY DEVICE: the number and position of the lines is the same in both panels, NO LINE MAY DISAPPEAR, only depth changes. Session variance applies to the PHOTOGRAPH, never to the FINDING.
  * ITS SELFIE EXTENSION: she must not come back better GROOMED. Each after-panel names what must survive - freckles, acne marks and under-eye shadows on f1; dry patches, broken capillaries and chapped lips on f2; active blemishes, oily skin and thick brows on f3.
  * NO CAPTION-SHAPED NOUNS. nbp_pro drew "FIRST VISIT"/"FOLLOW-UP" in r3, seedream drew "VISIT" in the full-face wave, and nbp_pro put text along the bottom edge again in selfie r2 even with the word removed entirely. The word appears nowhere here - verified by count before running - but nbp_pro reaches for captions on this brief regardless of wording, so check the frame edges on all of its candidates.
  * THREE NEW WOMEN, none used in any previous wave.
  * SKIN REALISM SPECIFIED POSITIVELY - pore size varying by zone, asymmetric never-mirrored pigmentation, vellus hair, greasy-to-dry variation. Sheen, glow, dewy and hydrated stay banned; they render as speckled white highlights reading as dry flaking.

KNOWN SUPPLIER STATE AT TIME OF WRITING: the Gemini pair is working again - Malcolm cleared the billing spending cap that returned HTTP 429 across the earlier selfie waves, verified by direct probe on both models. Luma refuses this brief family with HTTP 422 (five occurrences) because it has no negative-prompt field and the negative list folds into its prompt body; expect it to be absent. flux2 returns one candidate per call regardless of the flag and has twice produced watermark-like marks here, so check its frames at full size.

⚠️ NOTE ON CANDIDATE COUNT: generate-multi.py reads candidates from its --candidates CLI flag ONLY and ignores any `candidates` key in this config. A previous wave set 4 here and silently got 2. Pass it on the command line.

⚠️ PALETTE: a selfie cannot carry Acetyl's Pearl grey D8D6D4 studio ground without destroying the premise, so these blocks would lose the page's scene colour.
⚠️ SITE OF MEASUREMENT: all three trials measured the PERIORBITAL region, so a full-face frame shows more than the site measured. Block copy and alt text must not imply otherwise.
⚠️ RENDER SIZE: 660px desktop / 350px mobile split in two, so each face renders about 330px / 175px. Combined with the younger casting, the change may not survive the downscale. Judge at render size before choosing.

CLASS B, no references. Square 2048x2048, each panel a 1:2 portrait.

slots.title: f1 · Wang 2013 — 48.9% anti-wrinkle efficacy vs 0% placebo, 4 weeks  —  selfie, 30s
slots.prompt:
Two ordinary phone selfies of THE SAME WOMAN, taken WEEKS APART at home, placed side by side to fill one square frame edge to edge: TWO PANELS OF EXACTLY EQUAL WIDTH meeting at one crisp vertical edge precisely at the centre. Each panel is a tall portrait. The left panel is the earlier one, the right panel is the later one.

HER WHOLE FACE IS IN VIEW IN BOTH PANELS - head and shoulders, the entire face from above the hairline to the collarbones, nothing cropped off. Both eyes, the nose, the whole mouth and the full jawline are visible. Her expression is flat and unposed on both days, mouth closed, not smiling.

THESE ARE TWO SEPARATE OCCASIONS, NOT TWO COPIES OF ONE FRAME. Everything that identifies her stays the same, and everything a different day would change is different.

UNMISTAKABLY THE SAME WOMAN: the same face shape and jawline, the same nose, the same eye colour, the same brow shape, the same hair colour and cut, and her permanent marks - moles, freckles, blemish marks - in the same places on her face.

CLEARLY DIFFERENT BETWEEN THE TWO OCCASIONS:
  * PLACE AND LIGHT - on the earlier day she is in a bedroom in the evening with only the ceiling light on, a flat yellowish light straight down that puts shadow under her eyes; on the later day she is sitting by a window in flat grey afternoon daylight, much cooler and softer, with the curtain edge behind her. The two pictures plainly were not taken in the same room or the same conditions.
  * WHICH ARM AND WHAT ANGLE - she holds the phone differently each time, so the raised arm enters from a different corner and the camera sits at a different height relative to her face.
  * EYE GAZE - her eyes go to a different part of the screen each time.
  * BACKGROUND - a completely different part of an ordinary home, at a different brightness.
  * CLOTHES - a completely different everyday garment, a different colour and neckline.
  * HAIR - the same cut, unstyled, falling differently: a different parting, flatter on one day, flyaway strands out of place.

She must never stop being recognisably the same woman, and she must not appear older or younger, heavier or thinner, in one panel than the other.

IT MUST BE OBVIOUS AT A GLANCE THAT SHE TOOK THIS HERSELF. Every tell of a phone selfie is present and none of them is subtle:
  * HER RAISED ARM IS IN THE PICTURE. Her near shoulder is pushed up and forward and the top of her upper arm cuts into the bottom corner of the frame at a steep angle, because her hand is up holding the phone just out of shot. The line of that raised arm is the first thing that tells you what this is.
  * THE CAMERA IS CLOSE AND WIDE. The phone is barely more than an arm's length away, so the wide front lens exaggerates whatever is nearest it - her nose and chin read slightly large, her ears and the sides of her head fall away, and the background stretches behind her.
  * THE ANGLE IS NOT EYE LEVEL. She is holding the phone a little above her eyeline and looking slightly down at it, so her forehead reads large and her chin recedes.
  * HER EYES ARE ON THE SCREEN, NOT THE LENS. She is watching her own face while she takes it, so her gaze sits slightly below and to one side of the camera rather than meeting it.
  * IT IS BADLY FRAMED. The horizon is a few degrees off, she is not centred, and there is dead space on one side and none on the other.
  * IT IS A PHONE FILE, NOT A PHOTOGRAPH. Focus is imperfect, there is visible digital noise in the shadows, the indoor white balance is wrong in the ordinary way a phone gets it wrong, and the highlights clip.
There is NO MIRROR and NO REFLECTION, and the phone itself stays just outside the frame - only her raised arm and shoulder show.

SHE IS A WHITE EUROPEAN WOMAN of about thirty-eight, AND SHE IS AN ORDINARY PERSON RATHER THAN A MODEL. Cast her the way a real woman that age looks, not the way an advertisement casts: dark blonde hair scraped into a messy ponytail with flyaway strands escaping around her hairline, a round face with a slightly heavy jaw, hazel eyes, a scatter of freckles across the nose and upper cheeks, and a few faded acne marks along the chin and jawline. Her under-eye shadows are noticeable and her skin looks tired. Her features are asymmetric - one eye sits slightly lower than the other, her nose is not quite straight, and the two sides of her face do not match. She wears no makeup at all, her brows are natural and unshaped, and her hair is unstyled. Nothing about her is glamorous, and neither picture makes any attempt to flatter her.

SHE IS IN HER THIRTIES, AND THAT GOVERNS WHAT HER SKIN CAN HONESTLY LOOK LIKE. She has NO deep set wrinkles, no jowls, no sagging and no grey hair. Her lines are FINE and EARLY - the sort that have only recently started to stay put when her face is at rest. Anything deeper would be the wrong woman for the age given.

WHAT THE COMPARISON IS ABOUT, AND THE ONE THING THAT MUST BE TRUE: the number and position of the lines on her face is the same in both panels and NOT ONE OF THEM HAS DISAPPEARED. Her freckles, moles and blemish marks are all still there in the same places. What has changed between the two occasions is only HOW DEEP the lines are. She has not been made younger, slimmer, prettier or better groomed - the same ordinary face is simply less finely etched.

THE SKIN MUST HOLD UP AS REAL AND UNFLATTERED. Pores are clearly visible and vary in size and density by zone - open and obvious across the nose and inner cheeks, finer at the temples and jaw - with several individual pores larger than their neighbours. Pigmentation is uneven and asymmetric, never mirrored from one side to the other. Fine pale vellus hairs catch the light along the jaw and upper lip. The skin is greasy and light-catching across the nose and forehead and drier at the outer cheeks. No makeup on either day, so her lips, lashes and brows are their own natural colour and her under-eye shadows are her own.

ON THE EARLIER DAY, in the LEFT panel, her expression lines are fine but they are clearly there even with her face at rest: a small fan of three fine creases at the outer corner of each eye, two faint horizontal lines across the forehead, and a faint pair of short vertical creases between the brows. Under the hard overhead light each one holds a thin shadow.

ON THE LATER DAY, in the RIGHT panel, EVERY ONE OF THOSE LINES IS STILL THERE, IN THE SAME PLACES AND THE SAME NUMBER, AND NOT ONE HAS DISAPPEARED. Each is about HALF as finely etched - softer, holding a thinner and lighter shadow. The fan at each eye corner is still plainly visible. Her freckles, acne marks and under-eye shadows are exactly as they were.

A snapshot off a phone, not a photograph - slightly soft, slightly noisy, honest and completely unretouched.
